subject: Where customer data goes — console snippet + DPA Qs
messages:

Cc: procurement@acme.io

Subject: Quick ask — 'Where does my data go?' snippet for procurement

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement at ACME asked for two things before we can move to legal: (1) a one-paragraph plain-language snippet we can put in our vendor review doc titled “Where does customer data go?” and (2) confirmation about whether transient model caches or logging could result in copies leaving the EU.

They also attached a first-pass redline of the DPA — I’m attaching it here (ACME_DPA_Redlines_20280208.pdf) and included a short CSV of subprocessors we maintain for hosted API. Can you confirm whether the subprocessor list in your system matches what we’ll provide in the contract notice?

We’re on a tight timeline (legal wants this in 48 hours). Any chance you can propose text and a short bullet QA we can paste into our doc?

Appreciate it —
Sophie
Sophie Reed
Sr. Procurement Manager, ACME Corporation

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 'Where does my data go?' snippet for procurement

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the redlines and the note. I’ve pulled together two things below: a concise plain-language paragraph for procurement and a short Q&A addressing the EU residency / transient copy concerns. I’m looping in Laura (Sales content) and Marcus (Privacy product) to confirm we’re aligned with product claims and the DPA language.

Plain-language snippet (proposed for vendor review):
"Redwood Inference processes customer API requests in the region you select. For hosted API customers who choose EU residency, requests are routed to EU-hosted capacity and persisted only as required for billing, usage analytics, and optional (customer-enabled) logs. Model inference uses ephemeral caches on serving hosts; these caches are deleted on instance termination and are not treated as long-term customer data storage. Where we engage subprocessors (e.g., cloud regions, monitoring providers), we disclose the current list and notify customers in advance of material changes."

Short Q&A (paste into procurement doc):
- Q: Could my data be transferred outside the EU?
  A: By default, if you select EU residency we serve requests from EU capacity. Some operational situations (e.g., rare cross-region failover or remote debugging for critical incidents) may require temporary processing outside the EU. These scenarios are covered under the DPA’s cross-border transfer provisions and use standard safeguards (SCCs or equivalent).
- Q: Are inference caches or KV material replicated to vendors or subprocessors?
  A: No. The runtime uses ephemeral KV caches that are local to serving instances. We do not replicate KV caches to long-term storage or third-party analytics services.
- Q: What about logs and telemetry?
  A: Basic telemetry and aggregated usage metrics are retained for billing and platform health. We offer an option to disable certain logs for Enterprise/Private deployments; see the DPA appendix for retention windows.

I attached a console-friendly 1-line and 2-line variant (console-snippet-v1.txt) you can drop into UI cards or the procurement sheet. Marcus, any red-flag language in the snippet or Q&A vs the DPA?

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: console-snippet-v1.txt (txt)]

On Wed, Feb 8, 2028 at 11:03 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I attached a console-friendly 1-line and 2-line variant (console-snippet-v1.txt) you can drop into UI cards or the procurement sheet. Marcus, any red-flag language in the snippet or Q&A vs the DPA?

Thanks Irene — quick notes from product/privacy review: 
- The phrase "deleted on instance termination" is clearer if we say "removed from serving memory and not written to persistent storage" — avoids customers thinking we rely on VM lifecycle for deletion.
- For the cross-border line, let's avoid implying we do cross-border transfers routinely. Suggest: "may, in rare operational situations (e.g., emergency failover or critical debugging), be processed temporarily outside the selected region under DPA safeguards."
- Confirmed: KV caches are not replicated. Add sentence: "We enforce encryption-at-rest for any persisted tokens/metadata and limit access via role-based controls."

Ben, can you confirm the subprocessor CSV matches the list we publish in the console? If not, we should return an updated CSV and state the effective date customers see in the console.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Privacy Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the patience. Based on the reviews below we updated the proposed snippet and Q&A, and refreshed our subprocessor export. Key items for procurement:

- Copy (final):
"Redwood Inference routes API requests to the region you choose. For customers who select EU residency, requests are processed on EU-hosted capacity. Inference uses ephemeral caches on serving hosts; we do not copy those caches into long-term storage. Certain operational exceptions (rare failover or critical incident debugging) may result in temporary processing outside the region; such events are governed by the DPA’s cross-border safeguards."

- Subprocessors: we uploaded an updated export to the console (effective 2028-02-10). Customers see the effective date in the UI and we provide 30 days’ notice for material changes. EU residency customers will not be routed to APAC capacity unless there is an emergency failover.

- Next steps for ACME: 1) Laura — I’ve included a 1-line and 2-line console card for your procurement sheet. 2) Sophie — let us know if ACME legal wants the DPA redlines back with line-by-line commentary; we can do that by EOD tomorrow. 3) If you need an on-call privacy call for legal, we can schedule Marcus + Ben for a 30-minute sync.

Happy to finalize the DPA once we confirm ACME’s legal preferences.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
